summary: Pinned one callable Core OctoberBatchSetupPolicy constructor and PrepareAsync method, exact request/authority record construction, a subordinate writer port and closed OctoberPrepareResult statuses. Only Created/AlreadyIdentical return an exact committed selectable identity; every negative outcome returns no identity or capability. First-batch prepare remains separate from existing-batch BindAsync.
finding_disposition: The plan and shared contract name exactly one caller-facing Core setup policy, OctoberBatchSetupPolicy(IOctoberSetupWriter).PrepareAsync(OctoberSetupRequest, OctoberAuthorizedSelection, CancellationToken). The contract fixes its constructor, subordinate writer method, positional input records, OctoberPrepareStatus enum, OctoberCommittedBatch and OctoberPrepareResult. A test owner can construct the policy with a controlled writer and invoke the public method without inventing names, fields or a constructor.
feasibility: The concrete Core policy validates exact request/authority target, batch, Repository set and selection digest before the accepted Infrastructure writer may open the selected owned database. The writer remains the sole persistence owner and commits all setup-owned rows atomically; no additional setup policy, host route, tool or storage capability is introduced.
invariants: Created and AlreadyIdentical are successful only with a nonnull committed selectable identity matching request target/batch/digest and authorized canonical database identity. Conflict, Denied, AuthorityUnavailable, Cancelled and StorageFailure carry null identity and grant no selected-data capability. An exact identical retry observes the committed row without overwrite; a conflict never changes it. Cancellation before commit leaves no selectable batch, and acknowledged commit is not relabeled failure.
bootstrap_and_selector: Authorization-only Web still issues/validates a real grant without opening an October database. Generator prepare may invoke PrepareAsync after live validation and authorized empty-target migration without calling BindAsync. PrepareAsync does not issue a bound selected-data capability; generator select or selected-data Web calls the already accepted IOctoberBatchSelector.BindAsync only after an exact batch exists.
migration_and_compatibility: No change to fixed October schema, ordinary Web/Identity migration boundary, prepared-source approval tuple, Story 18.1 functions, provider binding or later-story exclusions. The new result is a Core contract shape, not implementation or database qualification.
constitution_and_architecture: The Core policy remains domain-only; the subordinate Infrastructure writer owns EF and transactions. The one shared policy avoids separate generator/Web setup rules and follows Constitution I/II/III and the accepted O-FR17/O-FR18 isolation spine without changing the PRD or adding a Worker tool/Scan strategy.
test_seam: A controlled writer can observe zero calls on denied/mismatched request or cancellation and return committed, conflict, unavailable or storage outcomes. T002's test author can name the exact policy constructor, input records and closed result; root must reconcile any task sequencing needed for a compilable behavioral RED rather than counting absent symbols as RED. Existing T001 work and external resource permissions are preserved.
implementation_design_shape: Architecture classification, single front-matter block, exact headings and existing design IDs are retained; ID-I01, ID-F02 and ID-T01 carry the narrow clarification. The installed deterministic plan-content validator returned no errors and git diff --check passed. Root owns state/path/hash-bound validation after mapping.
authority_and_gate: This plan correction does not itself restore suspended implementation approval or alter recovery count/pause. Root must repeat affected independent review and bind any applicable approval to corrected hashes before resuming implementation.
